change.title: AION Labs manufacturing establishment and maturation — six-stage programme
change.reason: Author-requested manufacturing programme: six overlapping subprocesses, role-based hires, direct predecessor inputs, technology/capability outputs and separate product maturity gates. New dates are proposed scenario choices for whole-group review. Preserve existing launch and stepper milestones; enrich and reparent the existing stepper programme instead of duplicating it. The 1983 parent end contains its existing shrink work. Mask-ROM is a scoped logic recipe within the existing schema. Correct the unrepairable launch DRAM criterion so repair is not backdated. Apply all elements atomically; existing authorizations and foundation records remain unchanged until approval.

after.name: AION wafer traceability, process control and yield engineering
after.description: Control of the Cambridge fabrication line through traceable lots, measured process windows, failure analysis and controlled recipe changes.

specification.description: Trace each wafer to material batch, tool, operator, recipe revision and electrical results; map defects and distinguish random from systematic failures.
Monitor particles, film thickness, sheet resistance, transistor thresholds, contacts and tool drift; use control charts and documented corrective action.
Separate engineering lots from released production; qualify maintenance and tool substitutions before customer manufacture.
Report wafer completion, electrical die yield, accepted speed/retention bins, package yield and good saleable chips per wafer separately.

after.name: AION memory characterisation and production testing
after.description: Wafer-probe, packaged-device and reliability tests supporting separate ROM, SRAM and DRAM release decisions.

specification.description: Qualify ROM image verification and SRAM read/write margins separately from DRAM retention, sensing, refresh and disturb behaviour.
Test across specified voltage and temperature limits; retain lot histories, wafer maps and failure-analysis evidence.
For repairable DRAM revisions, map defects, programme only supported redundancy and retest the complete device; unrepairable launch revisions receive no assumed repair benefit.

after.name: AION 3 µm customer-specific mask-ROM manufacture
after.description: Mask-ROM product recipe within the silicon-gate NMOS logic family; ROM-specific qualification does not qualify arbitrary logic or CPUs.

qualification_requirements.description: Customer-approved image, organisation, mask revision, package, timing and supply contract.
Repeatable wafer probe, full image verification, packaged test and reliability across independent lots.
Released order-specific masks and acceptance before customer shipments.

after.name: AION 3 µm SRAM manufacture
after.description: Small SRAM product-family capability, beginning with a 1 Kbit design and evaluating a separately qualified 4 Kbit extension.

qualification_requirements.description: Release each density, pinout, package and speed grade separately.
Read/write, standby leakage, data-pattern and voltage/temperature margins verified on multiple lots.
Production test coverage, package reliability and recurring cost per accepted chip.

after.name: AION 3 µm 16 Kbit DRAM manufacture
after.description: Cambridge recipe for the AION 4116-equivalent; production release precedes the June 1978 Aurelia launch.

qualification_requirements.description: Qualify capacitor, sense amplifiers, retention, disturb patterns and refresh across temperature and voltage.
Release 16-pin package, +12/+5/-5 V supplies, sequencing and measured speed grades against the product contract.
Demonstrate repeatable results across independent wafer lots, packaged final test and reliability screening.

after.name: AION 3 µm ERAv1 manufacture
after.description: Processor-specific fabrication, test and packaging capability. Initial release covers the 6 MHz part; 8 MHz requires separate measured qualification.

qualification_requirements.description: Frozen design rules, die and mask revisions, package/pinout, rails and power contract.
Functional vectors, timing across voltage/temperature, reliability and repeatable independent lots.
Record whether 6/8 MHz are speed bins or separate revisions; release only demonstrated grades.
Qualified launch inventory and production capacity before 19 May 1980; no dependence on later DRAM-control or sub-3 µm releases.

after.title: AION Labs manufacturing establishment and maturation
after.description: Establish Cambridge fabrication from the 1974 founding, develop commercial memory and repeatable 3 µm manufacture, qualify ERAv1 for the 1980 launch, and continue the existing stepper-led maturation through 1983. Adam funds capital and development; memory sales support operating costs without an assumed self-financing ramp.

inputs.description: The founding establishes AION Labs and its semiconductor investment mandate.

steps.description: 1. Establish the manufacturing team and pilot line.
2. Qualify commercial mask-ROM and SRAM manufacture.
3. Develop and qualify 16 Kbit DRAM.
4. Establish repeatable yield control and manufacturing discipline.
5. Develop 64 Kbit DRAM and continue the existing stepper programme.
6. Qualify 3 µm ERAv1 production for the 1980 launch.

outcomes.description: Cambridge process-control and test methods support separately qualified logic, ROM, SRAM and DRAM recipes.
The existing stepper programme delivers its separately dated smaller-geometry qualification outcomes.

after.title: Cambridge manufacturing team and pilot-line establishment
after.description: Recruit manufacturing leadership and establish a 75 mm silicon-gate NMOS pilot line with a 3 µm qualification objective. Use forgiving test structures during equipment bring-up.

inputs.description: AION Labs exists and can appoint staff and fund the Cambridge facility.

steps.description: Appoint the experienced manufacturing leadership and core integration team.
Purchase clean-area systems, ultrapure water, filtered gases, chemical handling and reliable temperature-controlled utilities.

Purchase and install Micralign projection lithography, resist coating/development, oxidation and diffusion furnaces, silicon/dielectric deposition, wet processing, metallisation, inspection and wafer probing.

Seek a licensed silicon-gate NMOS process-transfer package with training, design rules, test structures and reference wafers. Qualify the actual Cambridge route; a supplier or licence is not assumed from recruitment alone.
Hire equipment-maintenance, facilities, contamination-control and test technicians; contract supplier installation and training support.
Qualify 75 mm wafer handling and test structures; document process windows, tool acceptance and pilot electrical results.

outcomes.description: An accepted pilot line and documented process route support separate product qualification.

after.title: AION appoints its Cambridge manufacturing team
after.description: AION appoints a fab director, silicon-gate NMOS integration lead, lithography lead, facilities lead and test/reliability lead with production-ramp experience. Recruitment draws on established British, European and US semiconductor operations; individual names and former employers are unspecified. Supplier engineers train the new staff.

inputs.description: The founding authorises recruitment and investment.

outcomes.description: The appointed team takes responsibility for defining and qualifying the Cambridge process and its controls.

after.title: Commercial mask-ROM and small-SRAM qualification
after.description: Use customer-specific mask ROM and a modest SRAM family to establish repeatable fabrication, customer acceptance and an operating-revenue base. Sales quantities, prices and profitability remain unspecified.

inputs.description: The accepted pilot line can run product engineering lots.

steps.description: Hire ROM/SRAM product and applications engineers and a commercial lead for industrial controllers, instrumentation, terminals and peripherals.
Develop customer-specific mask ROM and a 1 Kbit SRAM; evaluate 4 Kbit SRAM only as a separate product qualification. Charge for ROM design/masks and seek minimum-order commitments.
Pursue licensed second-source contracts with explicit process-transfer, test, sales-right and customer-acceptance terms; no unexecuted licence or guaranteed customer demand is counted as income.
Install automated probing, memory testing, temperature fixtures and reliability ovens; initially qualify external assembly suppliers and retain AION final-test responsibility.
Qualify independent wafer lots and customer-approved ROM images, packages, timing and SRAM margins.

outcomes.description: Released mask-ROM and initial SRAM recipes provide commercial manufacturing experience and product-specific test methods.

outcomes.description: ROM/SRAM electrical, package and test evidence supports the released scope.

after.title: 16 Kbit DRAM development and production qualification
after.description: Build a dedicated DRAM team, establish capacitor and sense-amplifier behaviour with small test arrays, and qualify AION 4116-equivalent production before Aurelia launches in June 1978.

inputs.description: The pilot fab provides the platform for DRAM-specific process development.

steps.description: Recruit DRAM device, sensing and memory-test specialists.
Purchase ion implantation and annealing capability, and qualify the deposition/patterning sequence required by the selected capacitor structure.
Use small arrays or a 4 Kbit engineering vehicle to isolate leakage, sensing and refresh faults; an intermediate commercial release is not required.
Develop the 16 Kbit array and sensing circuits; qualify retention, disturb behaviour, supply sequencing, package and timing.
Extend temperature-controlled wafer and packaged testing, reliability screening and failure analysis; prove repeatability across independent lots.

outcomes.description: The 16 Kbit DRAM recipe and memory-test methods support Aurelia supply.

after.title: AION recruits DRAM process and test specialists
after.description: AION recruits a DRAM integration lead, capacitor/device engineer, sense-amplifier designer and memory-test lead with production experience. Offers include relocation, equipment budgets and long-term incentives. No named employee, former employer or proprietary transfer is presumed.

inputs.description: The operating pilot line gives the recruited specialists an executable development platform.

outcomes.description: Specialists establish the DRAM recipe and its retention, refresh and test requirements.

after.title: AION 16 Kbit DRAM production qualified
after.description: Independent lots of the AION 4116-equivalent meet released retention, refresh, timing, supply, package and reliability limits. The release supports manufacturing and inventory preparation for June 1978; no numeric yield is asserted.

inputs.description: The specialist team develops the DRAM recipe and verifies the production qualification lots.

outcomes.description: The released 16 Kbit DRAM process includes controlled recipes and complete production-test evidence.
AION 16 Kbit DRAM production qualified — production released

after.title: Cambridge yield engineering and production control
after.description: Turn recurring ROM/SRAM production into a controlled factory process, then extend the controls to separately qualified DRAM. Protect customer manufacture from experimental recipe changes.

inputs.description: Recurring qualified product lots provide failure maps and operational evidence for yield improvement.

steps.description: Appoint the permanent yield, failure-analysis and maintenance group.
Purchase film-thickness, sheet-resistance and transistor measurement equipment, improved inspection, and scanning-electron-microscope access; link wafer maps to lot histories.
Improve cleaning, filtration, gas purity, contamination monitoring and preventive maintenance; stock spares and duplicate bottleneck tools where justified.
Qualify plasma stripping and selected dry-etch operations layer by layer, controlling damage, residues and dimensions.
Run controlled experiments on implants, oxidation, annealing and contacts. Release improvements only after independent production lots pass electrical and reliability limits.
Measure wafer completion, electrical yield, accepted bins, package yield, good chips per wafer and recurring cost separately; do not count forecast yields as observed results.

outcomes.description: Repeatable 3 µm logic manufacture and controlled ROM/SRAM/DRAM routes support subsequent product ramps.

after.title: AION establishes a permanent yield-engineering group
after.description: AION appoints a yield manager, failure-analysis engineer, process-control engineers and maintenance specialists with authority to hold suspect lots and reject uncontrolled recipe changes.

inputs.description: Commercial lot histories establish the immediate need for systematic yield engineering.

outcomes.description: The team owns traceability, defect analysis, process windows and corrective-action methods.

after.title: Cambridge demonstrates repeatable 3 µm production
after.description: Independent logic test vehicles and released memory lots demonstrate controlled electrical distributions and stable production procedures. Product-specific timing, retention and package qualifications remain separate; no universal yield percentage is assigned.

inputs.description: The yield group establishes and verifies the production controls.
Released 16 Kbit production supplies the DRAM evidence needed for this cross-recipe review.

steps.description: Develop the larger array, capacitor, sense amplifiers, refresh and production tests on the existing 3 µm route; run engineering lots before stepper installation.
